ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, and ultimate beneficial owners against the Swiss SECO sanctions lists, UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN list, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the Swiss Money Laundering Reporting Office (MROS) PEP database. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for any politically exposed person (PEP), family members, and close associates. The screening must be documented and retained in the due diligence dossier for at least ten years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix – Central Business Name Index (www.zefix.ch) and the competent Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) of the registered office canton
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be written in an official Swiss language (German, French, Italian, or Romansh) or be accepted as a foreign-language name if it is capable of clear meaning in the Swiss commercial context. The required legal form suffix for a Swiss stock company is 'Aktiengesellschaft' or the abbreviation 'AG' in German; 'Société Anonyme' or 'SA' in French; and 'Società per Azioni' or 'SA' in Italian. The name must not be misleading, must not conflict with existing protected trademarks or company names, and must comply with Art. 950 et seq. of the Swiss Code of Obligations. Foreign words must be transliterated into Latin script and must not contain symbols or characters that are not recognized by the Swiss commercial register.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: In case of name rejection, the applicant must within the statutory appeal period file a written administrative objection (Einsprache) with the Cantonal Commercial Register Office that issued the refusal, stating the grounds and proposing corrective wording. If the commercial register office maintains its refusal, the applicant may file a formal administrative appeal within ten days to the competent Cantonal Economic and Labour Department or to the cantonal administrative court, depending on the canton. Further appeal to the Swiss Federal Administrative Court is available. An extension of an existing name reservation may be requested in writing before expiry, with a reasoned statement, and is subject to the discretionary approval of the commercial register authority.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office arrangements are generally permissible for an EMR SaaS company under Swiss law, provided that the registered Swiss seat is held by a licensed fiduciary, law firm, or commercial address provider that accepts legal mail and maintains the company's official registered address in the chosen municipality. The arrangement must ensure that company minutes, accounting records, and UBO documentation are physically or electronically accessible at the registered office. Some cantonal tax authorities may require a more substantive presence for VAT and corporate income tax registration; however, for a low-risk technology company, a properly structured virtual office is accepted as the registered seat.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for standard commercial registry matters (approximately 2-5% annual probability of an unannounced on-site inspection by the cantonal commercial registry or cantonal tax authority), but the risk increases to approximately 10-15% for healthcare-adjacent data-processing activities due to possible inspections by the Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner (FDPIC), the cantonal health authority (if medical data is processed), or FINMA in cases involving payment processing, notwithstanding the low AML/CFT risk classification.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (OR) Articles 629–641, Article 642 (minimum capital and payment), Articles 698–731 (corporate governance); Swiss Commercial Register Ordinance (HRegV), Articles 8–16; Medical Devices Ordinance (MepV) 602.115.0.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Swiss Federal Commercial Register (Handelsregisteramt / Office du registre du commerce), administered cantonal commercial register offices; central coordination by the Federal Commercial Register Office (FZR) in Berne.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public deed of incorporation (Statuten / Acte constitutif) with notarized signatures and a declaration of incorporation containing the founders, share subscription, and articles of association, filed as an electronic extraction to the Commercial Register.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum nominal share capital of CHF 100,000; at least CHF 50,000 must be paid up in cash at incorporation and deposited in a Swiss bank blocked ('escrow') account. A bank confirmation of the blocked funds must be submitted to the notary and the Commercial Register.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The Board of Directors, having reviewed the incorporation deed and the bank escrow confirmation, resolves: (i) to ratify the valid subscription and allocation of CHF 100,000 share capital, with CHF 50,000 duly paid into the blocked escrow account; (ii) to adopt and establish the company's registered office at [Street, City, Canton] in accordance with Article 2 of the Articles of Association; and (iii) to appoint [Name] as Chief Executive Officer and [Name] as Chair of the Board, with individual signatory authority, effective immediately and until the next shareholders' meeting. This resolution supersedes all prior inconsistent actions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and notarise incorporation deed and articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss civil-law notary (Notar / Notaire / Notaio) in the canton of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a notary in the selected canton. Finalise the German, French, or Italian articles of association reflecting the corporate name, share capital, registered office, corporate purpose, board powers, and number of shareholders. Summon the founders before the notary for execution; the notary authenticates the deed and verifies identity and capacity of all signatories.
required_dossiers: Founders' valid passports or Swiss identity cards
Founders' declaration on subscription and payment of share capital
Power of attorney if a founder is represented
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary rejects the draft for incomplete legal elements, revise the articles and re-authenticate within five working days; re-execution before the notary cures the formal defect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open blocked escrow account and obtain bank confirmation of paid-up capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss bank or licensed securities dealer recognised for blocked capital deposits
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a bank account in the future company's name with instructions that the deposit be declared irrevocably blocked for the benefit of the company until the Commercial Register registration is completed. Transfer at least CHF 50,000 of subscribed capital and obtain a formal bank blocking confirmation addressed to the notary and the Commercial Register Office.
required_dossiers: Bank account opening and blocking instruction forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the beneficial ownership structure, provide a clean corporate chart, definitive UBO declarations, and source-of-funds documentation; once clarified, the bank issues the blocking confirmation without further delay.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit electronic application to the cantonal Commercial Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / Office du registre du commerce) via the federal electronic extraction portal coordinated by Zefix
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized incorporation deed, articles of association, list of board members and authorised signatories, directors' declarations, and the bank blocked-funds confirmation with the Commercial Register of the canton where the registered office is located. Registration is applied for in the main register and upon completion confers legal personality.
required_dossiers: List of board members with signatures
Declaration of residence of directors (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Commercial Register queries name uniqueness, insufficient capital, or deficient signature specimens, the registry sets a cure period usually not exceeding ten days; file corrected documents within that period. A formal refusal may be appealed to the canton's civil court within thirty days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for federal taxes, VAT, and social security
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) for VAT; Cantonal Equalisation Fund / Compensation Office (Ausgleichskasse) for AHV/IV/EO employer contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After commercial register entry, apply to ESTV for a VAT number (Form 101) and to the competent cantonal compensation office for employer social-security registration. Declare the expected annual turnover and the nature of software services to obtain a definitive federal tax and social-insurance identification.
required_dossiers: Board resolution confirming principal place of business
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If ESTV queries annual turnover or the place of supply, submit a detailed revenue forecast and the cloud delivery model. If the compensation office rejects any officer appointment, correct the appointment declaration and re-file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt corporate governance framework and maintain statutory registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company Board of Directors exercising organisational autonomy; optionally notarized if share transfers or capital increases are resolved
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene an organisational board meeting to adopt the organisational regulations, assign executive responsibilities, establish signatory rules, open operational bank accounts, issue share certificates, and maintain the statutory share register and accounting records. Record all resolutions in minutes and retain at the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a bank or counterparty refuses to accept unsigned or uncertified minutes, notarize the board minutes and reissue certified copies; maintain a complete chain of resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce and complete closing formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (Schweizerisches Handelsamtsblatt / SOFC) publication via the Commercial Register Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the Commercial Register registration is granted, the registry automatically publishes a notice in the Official Gazette of Commerce. Verify the publication entry, retrieve the final commercial register certificate, update bank KYC files, issue statutory share certificates, and execute the corporate seal if required.
required_dossiers: Bank KYC update forms with final corporate documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Gazette publication is delayed or contains inaccurate data, notify the Commercial Register Office and request an amended publication; any typographical errors are corrected without adverse effect on legal standing.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Swissmedic (Swiss Agency for Therapeutic Products), with advisory role for medical-device software under the Swiss Medical Devices Ordinance (MepV) and the Health Insurance Ordinance for EMR modules; health-data aspects coordinated with the Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner (FDPIC).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Swissmedic conformity assessment registration and marketing authorization for medical-device software (Class I / IIa, if applicable) governing the sale of Electronic Medical Record workflow software to clinics; where clinical automation is non-medical-device, a formal Swissmedic non-application letter and privacy impact assessment are obtained.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN / BAFU / OFEV)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from mandatory environmental impact assessment for pure SaaS and software operations; not listed in Annex 1 of the Swiss Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (UVP/OEIA). If self-operated data centers or physical server rooms are established, an optional preliminary EIA screening may be required under cantonal law.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or Volatile Organic Compound (VOC) discharge for cloud software services; office servers and emergency backup generators must comply with Swiss federal air-pollution control thresholds (LRV/OPair), WEEE-compliant disposal of ICT equipment, and noise protection limits for managed equipment rooms.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Cantonal fire safety certification (Feuerschutzpolizei / VKF) for office premises including emergency lighting, exit routes, and fire alarm systems; structural load inspection for server racks if an on-premises data room is used; occupational health and safety clearance from SUVA and the Cantonal Labour Inspectorate for the registered office and any physical workstation facilities.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenoessische Steuerverwaltung ESTV; Administration federale des contributions AFC; Amministrazione federale delle contribuzioni AIV); VAT registration and returns: eService ESTV / SURE portal; UID register: https://www.uid.admin.ch; Customs export clearance: Federal Office for Customs and Border Security (BAZG/FOCBS).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Incorporate the AG in the Cantonal Commercial Register, which automatically issues the federal business identifier UID (CHE-XXX.XXX.XXX); the UID functions as the tax number. 2) File VAT registration with ESTV within 30 days once annual worldwide taxable turnover reaches CHF 100,000, or voluntarily under Art. 11 LTVA; use Form 800/801 or the eService portal. 3) A foreign entity without a Swiss establishment files Form 800 and, absent mutual administrative assistance or EU/EFTA establishment, must appoint a Swiss fiscal representative with joint and several liability. 4) The MWST/TVA/IVA number (CHE-XXX.XXX.XXX MWST) appears on all invoices and customs declarations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; the Swiss AG is an opaque resident company subject to unlimited worldwide income tax liability (Art. 50 DBG), with territorial exemption for foreign permanent establishments and foreign real estate that are actually taxed abroad (Art. 52 DBG). No Swiss tax-exempt zones or export-processing zones exist; effective federal+cantonal+communal headline CIT for an AG ranges approximately 14.0%-21.0% depending on canton and profit level.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Swiss law has no US check-the-box regime; the AG is per se opaque. Available elections: (1) Finance-branch election (Art. 51a DBG) allowing a Swiss branch of a foreign group with at least 51% foreign shareholding and at least CHF 10 million branch equity to be taxed as an independent Swiss subsidiary and claim participation relief; (2) Notional interest deduction on excess equity (Art. 25a VStG) with annually published rates; (3) Patent box election (Art. 24b VStG) granting a 90% exemption on qualifying IP and software-related income; (4) R&D super-deduction up to 150%; (5) VAT group election (Art. 13 LTVA) consolidating related Swiss entities into one VAT account; (6) Participation relief on qualifying dividends and capital gains from holdings of at least 10% or CHF 1 million market value.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Swiss Value Added Tax (Mehrwertsteuer/TVA/IVA) under the Federal VAT Act of 12 June 2009 (LTVA/MWSTG); a GST-style creditable consumption tax applied to Swiss domestic supplies, reverse-charged B2B services received in Switzerland, and B2C electronic services supplied to Swiss-resident consumers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 annual worldwide taxable turnover (Art. 10(2) LTVA as amended with effect from 1 January 2025; previously CHF 150,000); CHF 150,000 for non-profit and charitable organisations; voluntary registration below the threshold is available for businesses conducting an economic activity (Art. 11 LTVA), and foreign suppliers of e-services or B2B services to Swiss recipients must register once Swiss-sourced turnover exceeds the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland has no real-time fiscal clearance engine, no digital stamping requirement, and no mandatory API pre-clearance. Statutory invoice content is governed by Arts. 26-27 LTVA (supplier name/address/MWST number, supply date, description, consideration, tax rate and tax amount; simplified invoices below CHF 400). E-invoicing is admissible where data integrity, legibility and retention are guaranteed (Art. 26a LTVA); B2G e-invoicing with the Federal Administration uses Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 and Swiss eBill; no Continuous Transaction Control regime exists.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: the 0% export rate under Art. 23(1) LTVA applies when goods leave Swiss customs territory to a foreign destination; the export must occur in the month of supply or within the following five months and be evidenced by the customs export record. Services: 0% applies under Art. 23(2) LTVA for services directly related to exported or imported goods and international transport, and under Art. 23(3) LTVA for services supplied to a foreign recipient for the recipient's direct use or benefit outside Switzerland; in practice, cross-border B2B EMR SaaS supplies are outside the scope of Swiss VAT under the place-of-supply rule (customer's place of business, Arts. 20-21 LTVA), preserving full input VAT deduction, whereas B2C supplies to Swiss-resident consumers attract 8.1% Swiss VAT.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration with exit confirmation (BAZG e-dec-web/NCTS-CH) for goods
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill or CMR freight document according to transport mode
Sales or SaaS contract including Incoterms and delivery terms
SWIFT/MT103 remittance record or bank statement evidencing foreign payment
For EMR SaaS: signed master subscription agreement with the foreign clinic or hospital
Proof of offshore use: licensee deployment records, server access IP logs, and foreign VAT registration numbers of customers
Foreign entity confirmation or export-of-services substantiation questionnaire
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: No Swiss statute imposes an FX repatriation deadline; however, ESTV VAT audits (Art. 79 LTVA) verify export substantiation and the 10-year document retention obligation (Art. 88 LTVA). Where zero-rating is not proven, the supply is retroactively taxed at 8.1% with default interest of 4.5% per annum (Art. 75 LTVA); assessment limitation is 5 years relative and 10 years absolute, and VAT claims arising from tax evasion are not time-barred. Deliberate evasion triggers a penalty of up to three times the evaded tax (Art. 96 LTVA) and possible criminal fiscal-fraud prosecution (Art. 14 VStrR); procedural omissions are fined up to CHF 8,000 (Art. 87 LTVA). Voluntary disclosure before audit notification can reduce or waive penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (Schweizerische Nationalbank / Banque nationale suisse / Banca nazionale svizzera)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland maintains full convertibility of the Swiss franc for both capital and current account transactions. There are no exchange controls, no licensing requirements for foreign direct investment, and no restrictions on profit remittances or dividend distributions. However, distributions to shareholders are subject to Swiss withholding tax of 35%, which may be reduced or eliminated under applicable double taxation treaties if the recipient provides the required tax residence certificate. Foreign exchange transactions in CHF are completely free, but commercial banks may require accurate purpose codes and standard anti-money laundering declarations for high-value or cross-border transfers. No exchange rate margin or surrender obligation applies to any CHF conversion.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory surrender rules, mandatory conversion timelines, or minimum conversion ratios for export receipts in Switzerland. Export proceeds may be retained in any freely convertible currency, held in foreign currency accounts with Swiss banks, or converted into CHF at market rates without approval from the Swiss National Bank or any other governmental authority.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banca del Gottardo / Banca Stato (as regional alternative)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium. Offshore digital electronic money institutions (EMIs) that do not hold a Swiss banking license or FINMA fintech license cannot legally provide core payment or e-money services to Swiss-domiciled companies on a standalone basis. Such entities may provide support services through a white-label arrangement with a fully licensed Swiss bank or a licensed EU EMI that has passporting rights recognized in Switzerland. A Swiss FINMA-licensed fintech license (public deposits up to CHF 100 million without interest) is the most direct path for a regulated EMI vehicle, but this requires substantial substance, local audit, and compliance infrastructure. For the target SaaS entity, reliance on an unlicensed offshore EMI is not recommended in a regulated medical-data environment.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Swiss anti-money-laundering regulations do not impose a universal statutory requirement that directors appear physically. In practice, most tier-1 Swiss banks require a physical onboarding interview for non-resident corporate shareholders and directors on the first account opening, particularly for foreign-owned AGs. Some banks permit fully remote video identification if the ultimate beneficial owner already has a Swiss banking relationship or if the account opening is executed through a Swiss-regulated professional fiduciary (trustee, lawyer, or auditor) that conducts face-to-face due diligence. Retaining a Swiss regulated agent as introducer substantially improves onboarding success and removes the strict physical-appearance veto.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) chain involving non-EU shareholders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Organizational chart with full legal name, date of birth, nationality, and residence of every UBO; certified passport copies; recent utility bill or bank reference from an existing regulated bank; shareholders' register extract; and a written source-of-wealth statement signed by each UBO.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction classification of a shareholder or counterparty
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid FATCA and CRS self-certification forms, commercial explanation of the business reason for the jurisdiction link, evidence of real economic activity (contracts, invoices, payroll records), and a written no-sanctions-compliance opinion from a licensed Swiss attorney.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient source-of-funds documentation for capital escrow deposits
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements covering at least the last 12 months from the remitting bank, transactional ledger with counterparty names, tax returns or audited financial statements for the institution, notarized board resolution authorizing the capital transfer, and an audit-confirmation letter from a FINMA-licensed external auditor if requested.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Medical data / sensitive personal data processing as a beneficial activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Compliance pack including the Swiss Federal Act on Data Protection (FADP) registration certificate, appointed Data Protection Officer details, EU-GDPR representative evidence, ISO 27001 / ISO 27701 certifications, and a completed banking-sector KYC healthcare questionnaire confirming that protected health information is not transferred outside the EU/UK/Switzerland without lawful safeguards.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: trading revenues expected before first operational year
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Forecast P&L, board-approved budget, signed customer letters of intent, revenue model explanation, and evidence of the SaaS pricing contract pipeline; for any expected high-volume settlement, provide a treasury policy and AML transaction monitoring framework.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections to the Swiss AG must be routed via SWIFT MT103 or SEPA instant wire to the designated capital escrow account at a Swiss tier-1 bank. The remittance instruction must include the corporate purpose code (e.g., '10' for capital contribution under the Swiss National Bank's external statistics nomenclature, or the corresponding bank's purpose code for direct investment), the beneficiary legal entity name exactly matching the shareholders' register, and the reference to the notarized board resolution authorizing the share capital payment. For transfers exceeding CHF 100,000, the receiving Swiss bank will require proof of the remitter's identity, source of funds, and a fully completed form 'K – Konversion' only if FX conversion is requested. No exchange approval is required, but the bank must verify the UBO declaration under FINMA Circular 2016/1. Capital contributions made in foreign currency are credited at the current market rate; the bank's FX confirmation (deal ticket) must be retained as the official conversion evidence for subsequent tax audits.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound operational disbursements for software licenses, sub-processors, and international trade settlements should clear through SWIFT MT103 for high-value vendor payments and SEPA instant credit transfers for EU-zone operational payments. For procurement of hardware or licensed medical device components requiring documentary evidence, a Commercial Letter of Credit (LC) issued by the Swiss bank is permissible, with standard UCP 600 terms. Disbursement instructions require the corporate account Austrian/ISIC purpose code (including '10' for services and '02' for goods), plus supporting invoices and, where applicable, EU customs declarations. All outbound MT103 messages must reference the underlying commercial contract number and be accompanied by an anti-money-laundering tax-relevant declaration when the beneficiary is in a non-EU jurisdiction. Automated clearing in CHF or EUR is available via SIC / SEPA interoperable rails; USD settlements are processed via the bank's New York correspondent under CHIPS/Fedwire rules.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla deliverable foreign exchange forwards (FX forwards) for CHF/EUR and CHF/USD
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for exotic currency pairs where deliverability is not available, subject to bank approval
Cross-currency swaps (FX swaps) for simultaneous borrowing and lending in two currencies
Foreign exchange options (European-style) for premium-based hedging of transaction exposures

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal and cantonal corporate income tax return (annual tax declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal tax administration together with the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 March following the financial year for calendar-year taxpayers; extensions generally granted upon written request; in exceptional cases up to an additional 6 months
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Official ex-officio assessment, default interest (annual interest rate set by law), administrative monetary penalties up to 100% of evaded tax for negligent or intentional omissions, criminal sanctions for fraud; no direct commercial-register strike-off but a pending tax request can hinder cancellation or modification of registration

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Swiss VAT return (quarterly or annual declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration, VAT Division (ESTV / CFST)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 60 days after the end of each calendar quarter for quarterly VAT filers; 60 days after the end of the business year for authorized annual VAT filers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest, administrative penalty of up to 20% of the net VAT omitted (or up to 100% in severe cases), criminal sanctions for wilful omission; no direct strike-off proceeding

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual general meeting approval of the financial statements and appropriation of profits (AGM minutes and resolutions)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders; commercial register only if the meeting produces registrable changes (e.g., director resignation, share capital changes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the balance-sheet date (four months for listed companies); shareholders can resolve to extend this deadline in justified cases
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Shareholder petition to the court for an order to convene the AGM, director civil liability for losses caused by delay, and administrative order from the commercial register in case of persistent non-compliance; prolonged failure can lead to ex-officio dissolution and deletion from the commercial register

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary audit required for company groups and for any AG exceeding two of three thresholds for two consecutive years: CHF 20 million total assets, CHF 40 million net annual turnover, 250 full-time employees on average per year. A limited audit is required for all other AGs unless the company has fewer than 10 full-time employees and all shareholders unanimously agree to waive the audit for the given financial year.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (OR) statutory accounting standards; optional application of Swiss GAAP FER or IFRS; IFRS mandatory for companies whose equity securities are listed on a stock exchange.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Switzerland does not require an annual UBO confirmation filing to the commercial register or to any central beneficial-ownership register. An AG must maintain an accurate share register and must, under anti-money-laundering rules, identify and document the economic beneficial owner when the company engages in regulated business relationships. No periodic public UBO return is required.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors (internal record corresponding to the commercial-register entry)
Minute Book of General Meetings and Board Resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,500 - 5,500 (typical annual Swiss corporate services and registered-office provider fee)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,800 - 9,000 (market range for statutory limited audit of a typical small-to-medium Swiss AG)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% federal corporate income tax on post-tax profit (7.83% effective on pre-tax profit), plus cantonal/communal profit taxes; ordinary aggregate headline rate generally 11.9%-21.0% depending on Canton and municipality.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays; Switzerland grants patent box relief up to 90%, additional R&D super-deduction up to 50% on qualifying R&D and IP costs, capital-tax notional interest deduction in high-tax cantons, participation exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains, and tax-neutral repayment of paid-in capital reserves. There is no ordinary group tax consolidation at cantonal level, but a federal tax group regime applies since 2023.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Combined Federal and Cantonal Corporate Income Tax Return, official German/French designation 'Steuererklärung für juristische Personen' / 'Formulaire 110'; e-filed through the competent cantonal tax administration's secure electronic portal and transmitted to the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing deadline is generally within 6 months of the fiscal year-end; extensions are routinely granted up to 12 months after the year-end (for a calendar-year AG, frequently 31 December of the following year). If the taxpayer is in default after a final reminder, a 10-day grace period applies before official assessment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual net profit before taxes per statutory financial statements (Handelsbilanzgewinn).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident AG with a Swiss permanent establishment (PE) must enter only Swiss PE-attributable profit and attach an OECD-compliant profit attribution schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustments: hidden profit distributions, disallowed expenses, provision corrections, depreciation recaptures, tax-exempt participation income, capital gains.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only Swiss-source adjustments are permitted for non-residents; attach a reconciliation from PE statutory accounts to taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax loss carryforward calculation with year-by-year documentation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses of a Swiss PE may be carried forward for 7 years; losses realized outside Switzerland are not deductible unless a treaty PE applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Patent box deduction and R&D super-deduction calculation, including IP registration and R&D personnel costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only IP owned by the Swiss PE or Swiss AG and R&D activities actually performed in Switzerland qualify; attach supporting patent and payroll schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable capital (equity capital) for cantonal capital tax and paid-in capital reserve calculations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents with a Swiss PE show only the PE capital allocation; no separate capital tax applies for a foreign corporation absent a PE.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or obstruction of tax audit triggers a procedural fine up to CHF 10,000 under Art. 174 DBG; default interest at 3.5% per annum accrues on unpaid tax from the maturity date; if the return is withheld after a final reminder, the tax authority makes an official estimated assessment and may disregard unclear deductions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Transfer Pricing Documentation Form and Country-by-Country Report (CbCR) notification, filed via ESTV/SecureCenter and retained for inspection by the Swiss Federal Tax Administration.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; transfer pricing documentation must be contemporaneous and submitted only upon explicit request; CbCR notification is filed within 12 months after the reporting fiscal year-end.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: TP documentation must exist no later than the filing date of the corporate tax return. CbCR notification must be filed within 12 months of each group year-end; CbCR itself must be filed within 12 months via the automatic exchange of information mechanism.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Categories of controlled transactions with related parties: goods, services, IT/EMR SaaS licenses, royalties, interest, cost contribution arrangements, and counterparty jurisdiction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only transactions attributable to the Swiss taxpayer or Swiss PE must be reported; cross-border transactions with foreign affiliates require identification of the ultimate beneficial owner.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transfer pricing methodology and comparability analysis for each controlled transaction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Arm's length outcome under OECD TPG 2022 must be shown; local Swiss comparables should be used where available.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Intra-group services and management fees, allocation keys and markups.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For Swiss PEs, demonstrate actual benefit and use of services in the PE, arm's length reimbursement, and no duplication with head-office costs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Intercompany financing, shareholder loans, cash-pooling arrangements, and interest-rate determination.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include Swiss withholding tax analysis for bank deposits/bond instruments; provide credit rating, covenants, and functional analysis for each intercompany loan.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Non-production of records after request results in a procedural fine up to CHF 10,000; the tax authority may re-price transactions on an estimated basis, impose default interest, and, in case of false evidence, prosecute for tax fraud with imprisonment up to 3 years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% Swiss federal withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) on dividends and distributions from a Swiss AG; no separate cantonal withholding tax. Domestic qualifying shareholders may obtain a full refund; foreign shareholders must invoke a DTA or the Swiss parent-subsidiary directive to reduce or exempt the 35% rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief: (1) confirm the applicable DTA rate and Article 10 beneficial-ownership clause; (2) obtain an original Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) issued by the treaty-state tax authority for the actual payment year; (3) submit the Swiss paying agent a reduced withholding tax request using official ESTV forms (withholding tax notification/Bezüger form) before the payment is made; (4) if full 35% was withheld, file a formal refund claim with the Swiss Federal Tax Administration within the DTA deadline, attaching the dividend voucher, shareholder register excerpt, TRC, and beneficial ownership declaration. Relief is denied if the recipient is not the ultimate beneficial owner or if substance/anti-abuse rules apply.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: no Swiss statutory withholding tax on IP royalty payments; most Swiss DTAs reduce the royalty WHT to 0%. Interest: ordinary commercial and intercompany interest is not subject to Swiss withholding tax; however, Swiss bank deposit interest, bond interest, and money-market paper interest paid by Swiss residents are subject to 35% statutory withholding tax, generally reduced to 0% or 10% under DTAs, subject to Swiss anti-hybrid and substantive owner requirements.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Swiss TP documentation/local file is mandatory when aggregate controlled transactions with foreign related parties exceed CHF 10,000,000 per fiscal year; a Master File is required when consolidated group revenue exceeds CHF 900,000,000; CbCR is required above the same group-revenue threshold. Practical tax authorities may demand lower-de minimis documentation for financial transactions, IP flows, or management fees.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland does not codify a UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations regime, but the tax-avoidance doctrine, beneficial-ownership requirement, Art. 6 of the Swiss Federal Act on Direct Tax, and OECD MLI standards require genuine economic activity: operational premises, qualified personnel, decision-making powers, risk management, and actual corporate substance. An AG used merely as a conduit for EMR/IP licensing, clinic software revenue, or treaty-shopping royalties may be recharacterized as a shell, with DTA benefits denied and income attributed to the real beneficiary.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilfully declaring incomplete or false facts, suppressing turnover from clinic EMR licenses and SaaS subscriptions, producing false accounting records, or omitting taxable Swiss PE income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Procedural fine up to CHF 10,000 for obstructing authorities; evasion fine up to three times the evaded tax under Art. 175 DBG; qualified tax fraud with forged documents attracts imprisonment up to 3 years and monetary fine under Art. 186 DBG, plus default interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who sign false returns or order the omission are personally liable for tax penalties and fines; criminal convictions can include up to 3 years imprisonment, travel bans, and personal asset seizure; in insolvency, directors are jointly and severally liable for tax damages arising from negligence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Swiss AG without real office, employees, board decisions, or business risk allocation while licensing EMR software and receiving large royalties solely to access Swiss DTA benefits or protect profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority disregards the corporate entity, reallocates the income to the ultimate beneficial owner, refuses DTA relief, denies participation exemption and patent box benefits, and imposes full tax adjustment plus interest and procedural penalties up to CHF 10,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly allowed the empty structure to operate may be personally liable for unpaid taxes, restitution to creditors, prohibition from serving as corporate board members, and criminal fines or imprisonment in aggravated tax fraud cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the EMR clinical billing/payment rails to accept and transfer funds derived from criminal conduct, failing to identify beneficial owners of clinic counterparties, or deliberately omitting transaction-monitoring obligations under the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act (GwG).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Art. 305bis Swiss Criminal Code imposes imprisonment up to 3 years or a fine for standard money laundering; serious cases carry 1 to 5 years imprisonment; administrative fines under GwG can reach CHF 500,000; confiscation of criminal proceeds and forced winding-up of the legal entity can be ordered.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who participated in or authorized the AML breach face penal liability, asset freezes, bail restrictions, travel bans, and civil liability for damages suffered by creditors, investors, or the affected clinic network.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to withhold or remit the statutory 35% Swiss withholding tax on dividend distributions, bond interest, bank deposit interest, or constructive distributions to foreign or domestic shareholders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Art. 40 VStG, intentional violation is punishable by a fine up to CHF 30,000 plus the outstanding WHT and default interest; aggravated cases carry imprisonment up to 2 years and a monetary sentence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approved the distribution are personally and jointly liable with the company for the unpaid withholding tax; criminal conviction may lead to fines, travel restrictions, disqualification as director, and personal asset execution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare or maintain Swiss TP documentation when controlled transactions exceed CHF 10 million, overpaying management fees to foreign affiliates, or shifting EMR software royalties to low-tax jurisdictions without economic substance or arm's length comparables.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority can re-determine the taxable base using CUP, TNMM or Profit Split; disallow the deduction of the entire controlled payment, impose default interest of 3.5%, procedural fines up to CHF 10,000, and apply criminal tax-fraud penalties up to 3 years imprisonment if the documentation contains materially false statements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve or implement non-arm's length intercompany pricing are liable for damages in bankruptcy for breach of fiduciary duty; criminal liability attaches for deliberate false documentation, and Swiss courts may impose personal liability for tax penalties, restitution, and board disqualification.
